title: Tandem templating strategies facilitate the assembly of calix[8]arene-supported Ln18 clusters

synthesis.procedure: A mixture of H8TBC[8] (150 mg, 0.115 mmol) and LaCl3·6H2O (132.51 mg, 0.375 mmol) in 14 mL DMSO/MeCN (v:v = 1:1) was stirred for 5 min, then triethylamine (0.18 mL, 1.29 mmol) was added and stirring continued for 2 h. The solution was left at room temperature overnight to give a white precipitate, which was isolated by filtration and purified by slow diffusion of tert-butyl methyl ether into a CHCl3 solution of the product, affording colorless needle-shaped crystals.

synthesis.procedure: A solution of the dinuclear precursor La2 (314.45 mg, 0.15 mmol) and 1,3,5-tricarboxylic acid (15.75 mg, 0.075 mmol) in 8 mL CHCl3/DMF/MeOH (v:v:v = 3:3:2) was stirred for 5 min. NBu4OH (0.1 mL, 40% in water) was slowly added and the mixture was stirred for 1 h, then sealed in a PTFE-lined bomb and heated at 120 °C for 48 h. After slow cooling to room temperature, the cloudy solution was filtered to a clear yellow solution. Brown block-shaped crystals were obtained by slow diffusion of hexane into the mother liquor over four weeks. The paper notes that DMF is required and that syntheses under an inert atmosphere give the same product in lower yield.
synthesis.time: stir 1 h after base addition; 48 h solvothermal; crystallization over four weeks
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filtered after cooling to a clear yellow solution; brown block-shaped crystals by slow diffusion of hexane into the mother liquor over four weeks

synthesis.procedure: Prepared by the same solvothermal procedure as 1 (CHCl3/DMF/MeOH 3:3:2, NBu4OH, 120 °C, 48 h, PTFE-lined bomb), substituting the La2 precursor with the Nd analogue. The experimental write-up lists Nd as 134.50 mg, 0.375 mmol (the NdCl3·6H2O quantity used for the dinuclear precursor). Dark-green block-like crystals were obtained analogously (slow diffusion of hexane). Unit-cell checks confirmed 2 is isostructural with 1; crystals diffracted poorly so a full structure of 2 was not reported.

properties.summary: UV-Vis in CHCl3 matches the TBC[8] π–π* band near 304 nm. DC magnetometry shows χmT = 25.3 cm3 K mol−1 at 290 K, decreasing to 9.7 (0.1 T) or 9.0 (1.0 T) cm3 K mol−1 at 2 K, attributed to NdIII crystal-field depopulation plus predominantly antiferromagnetic exchange at low T. Magnetization at 2.0 K reaches 20.2 NAμB at 5.0 T (~34% of 58.9 NAμB saturation). No relevant ac out-of-phase signals (2–50 K, 3–1000 Hz, Bac = 3 G, zero dc field).

synthesis.procedure: Same general procedure as 1, replacing La2 with the Gd analogue and heating at 150 °C for 24 h instead of 120 °C for 48 h. The experimental write-up lists Gd as 139.38 mg, 0.375 mmol (the GdCl3·6H2O quantity used for the dinuclear precursor). After cooling and filtration, brown block-like crystals were obtained by slow evaporation of the mother liquor over four weeks. Unit-cell checks confirmed 3 is isostructural with 1; crystals diffracted poorly so a full structure of 3 was not reported.

properties.summary: UV-Vis in CHCl3 shows the ~304 nm TBC[8] π–π* band. Weak antiferromagnetic Gd···Gd exchange: χmT = 141.0 cm3 K mol−1 at 290 K, nearly constant to 50 K, then falling to 64.9 (0.1 T) or 59.1 (1.0 T) cm3 K mol−1 at 2.0 K; Curie–Weiss θ = −3.1 K. Magnetization 125.4 NAμB at 2.0 K and 5.0 T. No relevant ac out-of-phase signals. Magnetocaloric effect: −ΔSm = 23.7 J K−1 kg−1 and ΔTad = 8.6 K at 2.2 K and ΔB = 7 T (ca. 77% of 30.8 J K−1 kg−1 available entropy), described as the best calix[n]arene-based molecular magnetorefrigerant in this series.
